events.title: 1978: first large exodus
events.note: UNHCR's series for refugees from Myanmar in Bangladesh starts in 1978, the year of the first large exodus.

events.title: Myanmar citizenship law
events.note: Myanmar's 1982 citizenship law did not list the Rohingya among the recognised national groups, leaving most of them without citizenship.

events.title: 1991 to 1992: second exodus
events.note: A second large wave of arrivals. Returns to Myanmar followed from 1993, according to UNHCR's returns data.

events.title: Rakhine advisory commission reports
events.note: The Advisory Commission on Rakhine State, chaired by Kofi Annan, published its final report on citizenship, rights and development in Rakhine State.

events.title: August 2017: mass flight
events.note: After attacks by the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) and the military operations that followed, the largest flight of Rohingya to Bangladesh began. UCDP records an armed conflict between the government and ARSA in 2016 and 2017.

events.title: UN fact-finding mission report
events.note: The UN Human Rights Council's fact-finding mission on Myanmar reported on the 2017 military operations in Rakhine State and called for the military leadership to be investigated.

events.title: Joint registration completed
events.note: Bangladesh and UNHCR completed a joint registration of Rohingya refugees in Cox's Bazar; most received an identity document for the first time.

events.title: Military takeover in Myanmar
events.note: Myanmar's military seized power. UCDP records new armed conflicts in 2021, including with the National Unity Government (NUG).

limitations.text: Counted by country, not by ethnic group
limitations.detail: UNHCR counts refugees from Myanmar. The figures here are all refugees from Myanmar in Bangladesh, not only Rohingya.

limitations.text: Bangladesh has not signed the 1951 Refugee Convention
limitations.detail: Rohingya in Bangladesh are recorded through joint registration with the government; their legal status in Bangladesh differs from refugee status under the Convention.
limitations.to_check: wording on legal status (Bangladesh's own term for this group)

limitations.detail: Most Rohingya are described as stateless. UNHCR's stateless figures are a separate series and are not added to the refugee figures here.

limitations.text: Camps in Cox's Bazar and Bhasan Char are counted together
limitations.detail: UNHCR describes refugees in Cox's Bazar and on Bhasan Char island; the figures here are one national total for Bangladesh.

missing: births in the camps by year

refugees.reliability: Since the joint Government of Bangladesh and UNHCR registration completed in 2019, refugees in the Cox's Bazar camps are registered one by one with identity cards; earlier years rest on other counts.
